description: chennai menu rules — standalone (no `extends`), because inheriting Bangalore's ruleset keyed a third of its rules on flags Chennai's list leaves at 0. Chennai has NO welcome drinks at all (no `welcome_drink` course_type, `is_welcome_drink` = 0 across 361 rows), so every drink rule Bangalore ships was silently inert here. NOTE ON SCOPE: this is the engine skeleton plus the caps that are provable from the item list — it is NOT a transcription of a Chennai rulebook, because none has been supplied. Pune's 36 rules came from `Pune_menu_rulebook_101.xlsx`; the equivalent regional rules for Chennai (which kuzhambu on which day, poriyal/kootu rotation, rasam cadence) still need that document. Everything below is either universal engine behaviour or a cap whose selector was verified to match real Chennai items — see tests/test_chennai_rules.py, which fails if any rule stops matching.

rules._comment: 20-day item cooldown, same window as every other city.
rules.name: item_cooldown_20d

rules._comment: No dish twice inside one plan.
rules.name: unique_items_session

rules._comment: Don't reissue a week's whole signature within 30 days.
rules.name: no_repeat_weeks

rules._comment: Theme filter. `welcome_drink` is not in the exempt list because Chennai has no welcome drinks to exempt. `sambar`, `rasam`, `curd`, `curd_side` and `curd_rice` ARE exempt: they are the South Indian spine of every Chennai lunch and must survive a north or biryani themed day — without the exemption a north day filters the sambar pool to nothing and the slot silently drops. `dessert` is exempt for a measured reason: 26 of Chennai's 28 desserts are tagged cuisine_family=north_indian and only 2 (badusha, mysore_pak) south_indian, so a south day narrowed the dessert pool to TWO dishes and any week with 3+ south days was INFEASIBLE on uniqueness alone. The tagging is also wrong — payasam, semiya_payasam and all three kesaris are South Indian and filed north — but exempting the slot is the right fix regardless: a canteen dessert is not what makes a day South Indian, and the ruleset should not depend on 5 dishes being re-tagged to stay feasible. `bread` is exempt because the sample week contradicts theming it: Toast Tab serves CHAPPATHI / CHAPATHI / PARATHA on its South Indian days, but the filter narrows bread to the 10 south-tagged rows, which are the dosai and idly family — so a themed bread slot produced 'podi idly' as the bread row on a south day. A Chennai canteen serves chapati alongside a Tamil meal every day; bread is not what makes the day South Indian.
rules.name: theme_cuisine_filter

rules._comment: Colour variety. Chennai's list is brown-heavy — 194 of 361 rows (54%) are brown, against 67 red and 34 yellow — so Pune's flat cap of 2 per colour is too tight here: a day drawing 6 colour slots from a 54%-brown pool needs somewhere to put the third brown dish. This uses Bangalore's asymmetric shape instead: every colour capped at 2, with ONE colour allowed to reach 3.
rules.name: colour_three_distinct_one_colour_may_reach_three

rules._comment: Plain chapati/phulka may run on consecutive days — the same reasoning as Pune's R36. Chennai has 5 plain-chapati rows against a 29-dish bread pool, so this is less load-bearing here than in Pune (where the bread pool WAS the two chapatis), but a counter serving chapati daily still needs the cooldown exemption or week 2 has no chapati.
rules.name: plain_chapati_may_repeat

rules._comment: Rasam is a staple, and this one is load-bearing: the list holds exactly TWO rasam dishes (rasam, jeera_rasam) and a Chennai counter serves rasam most days. Under unique_items + the 20-day cooldown the slot is empty by day 3 of the first plan, never mind week 2. Rasam is the daily tamarind broth, not a variety slot — the same call as steamed rice.
rules.name: rasam_is_a_staple

rules._comment: Curd and raita are staples, for the reason Pune's raita_is_a_staple documents: 4 curd_side rows (plus 1 plain curd) against a slot served daily. A yogurt side is an accompaniment, not variety.
rules.name: curd_and_raita_are_staples

rules._comment: Curd rice likewise — the list holds 2 (curd_rice, dry_fruits_curd_rice) and Toast Tab serves it on every flavoured-rice day.
rules.name: curd_rice_is_a_staple

rules._comment: One premium veg gravy a week (25 eligible rows). Cost rule, same as Pune's.
rules.name: premium_gravy_weekly

rules._comment: One premium veg dry a week (7 eligible rows).
rules.name: premium_veg_dry_weekly

rules._comment: At most one premium veg dish on any single day, so the two weekly premiums cannot stack onto one plate.
rules.name: premium_veg_daily_max_1

rules._comment: One mixed-veg pulao or veg biryani a week in the rice slot (8 + 4 rows).
rules.name: mixedveg_pulao_biryani_weekly

rules._comment: One non-veg biryani a week (5 rows). Chennai's non-veg pool is 63 dishes, so this leaves plenty for the other days.
rules.name: nonveg_biryani_weekly

rules._comment: At most one non-veg biryani on a day, so a multi-slot non-veg counter cannot satisfy the weekly cap by stacking two onto one day (the trap note 9e documents).
rules.name: nonveg_biryani_daily_max_1

rules._comment: One maida (refined-flour) bread a week — 15 rows, so this is a real constraint on a 29-dish bread pool.
rules.name: maida_bread_weekly

rules._comment: Baby corn once a week. Matched on the dish NAME, not `key_ingredient` — in Chennai all 4 baby-corn rows agree on both, but Bangalore's list showed key_ingredient='baby_corn' is the de-facto default for a mixed salad (67 rows, 3 of them actually baby corn), so the name is the trustworthy column across cities.
rules.name: baby_corn_weekly

rules._comment: One leafy veg dry a week (4 rows: keerai and mint dishes).
rules.name: leafy_veg_dry_weekly

rules._comment: Kootu at most twice a week. Chennai-specific and only expressible because `kootu` is its own sub_category (7 rows) — `course_type` files kootu under veg_gravy alongside the kurmas, so a course_type selector could not separate them. Two rather than one because kootu is an everyday Tamil dish, not a treat.
rules.name: kootu_twice_weekly

rules._comment: One chana gravy a week (4 rows).
rules.name: chana_gravy_weekly

rules._comment: Dal colour must not repeat on adjacent days.
rules.name: dal_colour_non_consecutive

rules._comment: Each sambar key ingredient at most twice per horizon — the 7-dish sambar pool would otherwise rotate two vegetables all week.
rules.name: sambar_key_ingredient_max_two

rules._comment: Vary the dessert form across adjacent days (halwa / payasam / kheer / laddu).
rules.name: dessert_form_non_consecutive

rules._comment: Vary the veg gravy's key ingredient across the week.
rules.name: veg_gravy_key_ingredient_variety

rules._comment: Same for the veg dry.
rules.name: veg_dry_key_ingredient_variety

rules._comment: Don't run South Indian chicken gravies on consecutive days (10 rows) — soft, so it yields when the non-veg pool for a themed day leaves nothing else. Was 11 until fish_kuzhambu stopped being flagged is_south_chicken_gravy: it is a fish, and scripts/seafood_taxonomy.py cleared the chicken flags off the 8 seafood rows.
rules.name: avoid_consecutive_south_chicken

rules._comment: Seafood weekly ONCE — confirmed by the client, replacing the 2 I had inferred from the sample. `max` counts DAYS, not dishes, so with one nonveg_main slot this is one fish dish a week; a counter with 2+ nonveg slots could still stack two fish onto that one day, which `daily_max` would be the fix for if it ever matters here. Exists mainly so the seafood flags are load-bearing: Chennai is the first city list with fish, and `is_seafood` is the umbrella (`is_fish_dish` is the fish-only subset, so prawn or crab in a future list is covered without touching this rule). Drop or widen this once a Chennai rulebook states the real rate.
rules.name: seafood_weekly

rules._comment: Same for North Indian chicken gravies (13 rows).
rules.name: avoid_consecutive_north_chicken

rules._comment: Keep the week's two premiums on different days.
rules.name: premiums_different_days

rules._comment: Paneer belongs on a mix / south / north day; chinese and biryani days are the fallback, not the default (client rule, all cities). SOFT on purpose: the hard equivalent is selector_frequency.allowed_day_types, which forbids paneer on the other days outright — and a counter themed chinese or biryani every weekday would then never serve paneer at all.
rules.name: paneer_prefers_mix_south_north_days

rules._comment: No soya, baby corn, chole or mushroom on a paneer day (client rule, all cities) — they read as substitutes for each other, so serving two wastes a slot. Counted across every slot because the point is the day's plate. Baby corn matches on the dish NAME for the reason baby_corn_weekly explains. A dish satisfying BOTH sides (a paneer chana gravy) counts as paneer only, otherwise `a + b <= 1` reads `1 + 1 <= 1` and the dish becomes unservable.
rules.name: paneer_not_with_soya_babycorn_chole_mushroom
